name: Kangaroo Island Wilderness Trail
objection: Named by the tourism board as a well-known multi-day trail through Flinders Chase (a Great-Walk style long trail, campsites on route); a long trail is a spot.

name: Flinders Chase National Park
objection: Wikivoyage and agency: Kangaroo Island's flagship national park (Remarkable Rocks, Admirals Arch, wildlife) with an entry fee; a place in its own right.

name: Remarkable Rocks
objection: Wikivoyage See: wind-sculpted granite formations you can walk among, Flinders Chase; headline draw.

name: Admirals Arch
objection: Wikivoyage See: rock arch with New Zealand fur seal colony reached by boardwalk and steps in Flinders Chase; headline draw.

name: Cape du Couedic Lighthouse
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under Lighthouses and the board names it with Admirals Arch; remains of storerooms and flying fox a short walk away. Exterior only, but a guide-singled-out landmark.

name: West Bay
objection: Tourism board singles out West Bay as the island's westernmost inlet at the Rocky River mouth, with sea views and wildlife; a bay a guide names.

name: Hanson Bay
objection: Two counted sources: board says watch the Southern Ocean roll in and beach-walk the dunes to three beaches. (Candidate coordinates are a NZ Hanson Bay: wrong, resolve afresh.)

name: Cape Borda Lighthouse
objection: Wikivoyage lists the 1858 Cape Borda Lighthouse with tours; remote but a named lightstation to visit.

name: Ravine des Casoars
objection: Wilderness protection area beside Cape Borda that the board names for exploring the Valley of the Cassowaries (hiking trail).

name: Kelly Hill Caves
objection: Wikivoyage lists Kelly Hill Caves show-cave tours (daily, fee) in Kelly Hill Conservation Park.

name: Seal Bay Conservation Park
objection: Wikivoyage See: Australian sea lion colony with guided beach tours, daily; headline draw.

name: Little Sahara
objection: Wikivoyage Do: Little Sahara sandboarding dunes on the South Coast Road.

name: Vivonne Bay
objection: southaustralia.com and Wikivoyage: long white beach once voted among Australia's best, jetty, south coast tour stop.

name: Harriet River
objection: Board names the calm river near Vivonne Bay for swimming and kayaking with koala and echidna spotting; distinct from the beach.

name: D'Estrees Bay
objection: Two counted sources: surf and fishing beaches with south coast scenery, a favourite of surfers.

name: Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park
objection: Parks SA and the board name the park (wilderness area, walking trails, D'Estrees Bay southern section, Murray Lagoon). Kept as a park with named walks.

name: Murray Lagoon
objection: Wikivoyage and the board name it: wetland with Bald Hill and Timber Creek half-hour to hour walks for birdwatching.

name: Pennington Bay
objection: Wikivoyage says 'don't miss Pennington Bay' and the board features the view; a surf beach on the south coast.

name: Prospect Hill
objection: Both sources: 500-step climb to a 360-degree view, Flinders ascended it in 1802.

name: American River
objection: Both sources give the fishing village its own section: wharf, Independence replica and rebuild shed, walks, wildlife, oysters.

name: Kingscote
objection: Wikivoyage and tourism board give Kingscote its own section: island's largest town, harbour and first European settlement of South Australia.

name: Reeves Point
objection: Both sources: site of South Australia's first settlement, lookout, famous Mulberry Tree, interpretive signs.

name: Hope Cottage National Trust Museum
objection: Board names the museum's 'outstanding collection' of island heritage in an 1856 cottage; small museum visitors can enter.

name: Kingscote Silo Art
objection: Board features the 25 m kangaroo and glossy black cockatoo silo mural ('you can't miss'); a roadside icon.

name: Kingscote Jetty
objection: Board names the jetty for fishing, sunset and snorkelling for leafy sea dragons around the pylons; a jetty a guide names.

name: Kingscote Pelican Feeding
objection: Wikivoyage names the free daily 5pm pelican feeding behind the Marine Centre as a Kingscote wildlife stop; permanent daily activity, about half an hour. Objection: a scheduled daily feed rather than a place.

name: Duck Lagoon
objection: Tourism board and Wikivoyage name it: koalas, bird hide, walking trail around the lagoon to old eucalyptus distillery ruins and picnic area.

name: Kangaroo Island Wildlife Park
objection: Wikivoyage See: walk-through wildlife park near Parndana with kangaroos coming to visitors.

name: Parndana
objection: Tourism board gives Parndana its own destination page (central base, Soldier Settlement Museum, Australian Red Gum Gallery) and Wikivoyage lists it as one of four settlements; kept as a town, though thin.

name: Parndana Soldier Settlement Museum
objection: Tourism board names this small historical display on the soldier settlement scheme on the edge of Parndana; open museum, about 30 min. Objection: small, one-source museum.

name: Emu Bay
objection: Tourism board names the 4 km white sand safe swimming beach with 100-year-old jetty and boat ramp; also covers the Emu Bay trilobite fossil shale (Emu Bay Shale merged here).

name: Stokes Bay
objection: Tourism board: beach reached through a boulder cave tunnel, rock pools; named Australia's best beach 2023.

name: King George Beach
objection: Tourism board names this pebbly cove beach, known for colour at sunset. Objection: brief mention, one source.

name: Snellings Beach
objection: Tourism board names it for swimming, surfing and fishing at the mouth of Middle River. Objection: brief mention.

name: Western River Cove
objection: Tourism board and Wikivoyage name it: beach and campground beneath cliffs at the Western River mouth, glossy black cockatoo habitat.

name: Penneshaw
objection: Wikivoyage settlement and ferry arrival point with the Gateway visitor centre; tourism board has a Penneshaw and Dudley Peninsula section (penguin centre, museum).

name: Penneshaw Penguin Centre
objection: Wikivoyage and tourism board ("don't miss the little penguins, best on a night tour"): the Penneshaw little penguin colony at Lloyd Collins Reserve, a permanent nightly experience. Objection: access is by guided tour from an operator.

name: Penneshaw Maritime and Folk Museum
objection: Wikivoyage lists it and tourism board describes a National Trust museum with maritime and folk displays; small museum a guide names.

name: Hog Bay
objection: Tourism board names Hog Bay beach at Penneshaw as a swimming and fishing beach. Objection: brief mention.

name: Kangaroo Island Sculpture Trail
objection: Tourism board lists the new outdoor sculpture trail near Penneshaw under natural attractions; open walk. Objection: new, one source.

name: Ironstone Hill Hike
objection: Parks SA and tourism board: coastal trail to the Bates family cottage ruins, whales in season, glossy black cockatoos; walk visitors do.

name: Cape Willoughby Lighthouse
objection: Wikivoyage lists South Australia's first lighthouse (1852) with tours to the top; agency page confirms visitor centre and views.

name: Cape Willoughby Conservation Park
objection: Parks SA visitor page: state's oldest operating lighthouse, daily visitor centre, tours and coastal walks; Wikivoyage lists the lighthouse. Treat as one place with Cape Willoughby Lighthouse if that is also a candidate.

name: Lashmar Conservation Park
objection: Parks SA and tourism board: Chapman River canoeing, fishing, swimming at Antechamber Bay, picnic area and camping.

name: Waterfall Creek Hike (Flinders Chase)
objection: Named DOC-style walk in Flinders Chase on the tourism board page: trail down to a creek, stepping stones and a lookout over a seasonal waterfall, from the Western River car park on Colmans Rd. Distinct walk; worth an hour. Seasonal waterfall.

name: Return Road Hike (Flinders Chase)
objection: Named walk on the tourism board page: lightkeepers' old cart track between Harveys Return and Cape Borda through sugar gum woodland past the lightkeepers' cemetery, can extend to the Clifftop lookout. Hours-long distinct walk.

name: Harveys Return Hike (Flinders Chase)
objection: Named walk on the tourism board page following the lightkeepers' original route toward Cape Borda with ocean views; steep sections. Distinct walk; overlaps partly with Return Road Hike (same corridor) but is its own named route. Flinders Chase page on parks.sa.gov.au is the managing agency.

name: Penneshaw Beach
objection: Tourism board names this 600 m town beach (Hog Bay) with picnic facilities, a swim and a monument to the French explorers; a harbour-town beach is a second-tier stop. Only one counted source and a short visit but beaches a guide names are kept.

name: Red Banks Beach
objection: Tourism board names the colourful red-orange cliffs 15 min north of American River, best at sunset; a second-tier scenic stop. Minimal facilities.

name: Point Ellen
objection: Tourism board names the Vivonne Bay western headland for coastal scenery, crashing Southern Ocean waves and turquoise rock pools to swim in (swell warning). Second-tier headland a guide names.

name: Fireball Bates Walking Trail
objection: Tourism board names a 3 km easy interpretive loop (1-2 hours) from the visitor centre in Penneshaw to near the ferry, with signs on settler George Bates. Named walk.

name: Frenchmans Rock
objection: Tourism board names the rock inscribed by Baudin's crew in 1803 at Penneshaw, an historic monument; short stop but a named historic landmark. Close to Penneshaw Beach (monument at eastern end), so a modest one.

name: Tadpole Cove Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
objection: Agency-sourced walk (DEW/NPWS) to a lookout above Tadpole Cove past early-settler threshing floor and cottage ruins; osprey watching. Distinct named walk.

name: Timber Creek Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
objection: Agency-sourced walk at Murray Lagoon in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park for swamp birdlife (ducks, swans, waders); named walk. Seasonal flooding in winter. Overlaps the Bald Hill/Curley Creek area but is a separate trail.

name: Curley Creek Hike (Cape Gantheaume)
objection: Agency-sourced hike along Murray Lagoon edge in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park (6 km from park office) with birdlife and vegetation; named long walk, distinct from Bald Hill walk. Winter flooding.

name: Beyeria Walk
objection: Agency-sourced 1.5 km, 30 minute interpretive mallee walk (20 signs) in Beyeria Conservation Park; named walk.

name: Brown Beach
objection: Tourism board names a sheltered, easily accessible family beach for swimming, snorkelling and shell fossicking with camping ground, BBQs and toilets; second-tier beach.

name: Bales Beach
objection: Tourism page: accessible surf and walking beach next to Seal Bay inside an aquatic reserve protecting sea lion breeding; small car park. Second-tier beach, short stop.

name: Bald Hill Walk (Cape Gantheaume)
objection: Agency-sourced walk to Bald Hill with spectacular views over Murray Lagoon and wetland bird watching in Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park.
